broader_coverage.reasoning: The unrestricted-length source with most similar model computes whether a needle hits any grid line, not how many lines it hits. The general-dimensional variance theorem is restricted to short needles, so it cannot dominate the claimed long-length asymptotic.

correctness.rationale: Uniform independent phases give conditional crossing variances g(u),g(v). The law of total variance and the exact angular moments produce the stated quadratic coefficient and negative family covariance. The absolutely convergent Bernoulli-polynomial Fourier series and the Bessel integral identity yield the exact all-length variance. Uniform large-argument Bessel errors sum as O(L^-3/2). Integer/half-integer substitutions yield opposite nonzero limits; independent quadrature and direct sampling agree. Null grid-vertex events and fixed-spacing limits are explicit.

originality.rationale: Full text of the most relevant unrestricted rectangular-grid works derives first moments, maxima or hit indicators rather than count variance; the direct high-dimensional variance source is short-regime only. Neither indexed geometry comparisons nor targeted web search revealed the all-length two-family Bessel variance and phase-sensitive L^-1/2 term. Parallel-line long-needle moments in the partially accessible 1976 source remain a named historical risk; priority is provisional, not independently certified.

value.rationale: The variance of visited-tile or crossing count is a natural second-order observable for the well-studied Buffon-Laplace experiment and for long-needle estimators. The sharp oscillating correction exposes length/grid resonance invisible from the classical mean or leading quadratic variance. The result covers every positive length and rectangular aspect ratio and supplies strictly distinct integer versus half-integer asymptotics, not an arbitrary computation.
